clinician.final_diagnosis: Immediately after diagnosing chickenpox in the non-VZV-vaccinated girl combined with bullous impetigo and hypopyon sign due to Staphylococcus aureus superinfection on the basis of atopic skin and VZV infection, the patient was isolated in the pediatric ward and received acyclovir 130 mg TID (10 mg/kg/day) and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 650 mg TID (50 mg/kg/day) intravenously for 5 days.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A three-year-old girl with a history of mild atopic dermatitis presented with high-grade fever and a new skin rash characterized by generalized blisters, some with hypopyon sign, erosions, papules, vesicles, pustules, and crusts. VZV infection was confirmed by positive Herpes PCR from serum and blisters. Bacterial superinfection with Staphylococcus aureus (non-methicillin resistant) was identified from a skin smear culture. The patient was non-VZV-vaccinated. She was isolated and treated with intravenous acyclovir and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid for 5 days, along with supportive care including parenteral fluids, paracetamol, and oral antihistamines. Treatment was then switched to oral therapy for an additional 5 days, and topical treatments were also applied. The patient recovered completely, with only some eczema plaques persisting.

She recovered completely, only some eczema plaques persisted from the known AD.
